title: The Curve Is the Material — rich
forward_vector: I am the manifest of The Curve Is the Material's rich face, its first round, a Sketch and still a proposal: one walk that starts on the flat harmonic line and ends on a measurement of the section's distinction, between morphing a stiff string's one number and blending its two end curves point by point. I grow when the page is enriched again, toward the function picker its forward vector asks for; I never hold the entry's words.

offers.what: An emphasis, quantified; the text's "may" already stands. Blended point by point in cents, the way Wavetable B frames are scanned, the section's own pair 0.001 → 0.003 is never one string between its ends: at t = 0.5, partial 1 reads B = 0.00200 and partial 24 reads 0.00186. But its worst partial stays within 1.56 ¢ of a real string at 16 partials, 4.03 ¢ at 24 and 12.3 ¢ at 64, which is 0.5–0.7 % of the stretch it carries (fit with B and f₀ both free; the challenger reproduced these independently). The gap grows as the ends move apart and the partials go higher: 0.0002 → 0.004 gives 15.7 ¢ at 24 partials and 65.3 ¢ at 64; 0.001 → 0.1 gives 149 ¢. Suggest the paragraph give the size. Two limits: the bound holds only when both frames are strings, and freely drawn frames have none; and whether a few cents is audible wasn't checked.

The third paragraph sets function-type interpolation ("the weighted sum of two real physical models") against arbitrary curve blending, but a weighted sum taken partial by partial is the curve blend the first paragraph warns about. The piece shows that the blending is what makes the departure from a physical model, and the two ends set its size: the same point-by-point blend is 4 ¢ off a string between 0.001 and 0.003 and 149 ¢ off between 0.001 and 0.1, while the number morph between the same ends stays at 0. So the paragraph's distinction holds only for a path through one unified family, which is what Open Questions' "string-to-bell morph function" asks for, and the paragraph could point there. A string-to-Bessel blend also has to choose an order for the membrane's (m, k) modes before "partial n" means anything. This is reasoning from the piece; that blend was not measured.

offers.section: Design Implication: Function Library Over Freehand Curve
offers.what: Calculated on the coefficient formula B = π³·E·d⁴/(64·T·L²), not tested by a piece. A plain steel string of 0.775 mm, 51 mm long, at 700 N (assumed dimensions; f₀ = 4263 Hz, close to C8) gives B = 0.0192, so the top of a piano crosses "B > 0.01: no real material" (the challenger recomputed it). Separately, 0.004 as a "heavy piano bass string" looks high for a bass string: the palace's own May proof (Piano String Inharmonicity, proofs/2026-05-04-B-slider.html) gives 0.004 as a treble value, and Projects/Piano String Inharmonicity.md gives 0.0001–0.001. B is lowest mid-keyboard and rises toward both ends, much more steeply in the treble. The palace's three ranges disagree, so a sourced range is still wanted before this goes home.

Calculated, not tested by a piece. "Hyper-stiff strings with B = 0.1 produce inharmonic spectra nothing physical ever generates": by the coefficient formula, a 1.5 mm steel wire 10 cm long at 500 N (283 MPa, well inside music wire's strength) has B = 0.098 and sounds near 950 Hz. As B·n² grows, the formula's partials go as n², the series of a bar pinned at both ends (Inharmonic Wavetable Synthesis already plays that string-to-bar morph). So the hyper-stiff string is a short, thick, tight wire on its way to a bar, a real object. The section's point that the constraint is generative stands; the 'nothing physical' clause doesn't.

pieces.title: two ways to morph a string · a walk in five steps
pieces.caption: **Does blending the curves leave the family, and by how much?** The flat harmonic line, bowed by one number B; then a way to read the stiffness back off every partial, where a real string reads one B from all of them; then the section's two strings, 0.001 and 0.003, morphed by the number; then the same two blended partial by partial, where the reading tilts from the average at partial 1 toward the geometric mean at the top; and last the test, every point of both morphs measured against the nearest real string. The number's morph stays a string. The blend leaves the family, but between the section's own pair only by about 4 ¢ at 24 partials; the gap opens as the strings move apart and the partials go higher. See the offers on this section.
